id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional intra-Realm Circle (models/circle.md) defining this Relation fact's effective scope, supplied in the submit payload. For confidential_discussion_of it points to the private Strand's Circle. For structural relations the resulting effective_scope MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope (circle.md §6.1). Sidecar context mappings are native sidecar.context typed results, not Relation objects.

effective_scope.description: Read-only immutable effective scope of this Relation fact, materialized from the accepted Event.scope_ref after the receiver verifies it against scope_circle_id and endpoint pre-state (circle.md §6.1-§6.2). For structural relations it MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope. It remains immutable across any later scope rebind and MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied content payload (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).

relation_kind.description: Relation semantic. The standard kind vocabulary (kind list, cardinality class, truth-source class, weak_semantic flag) is machine-indexed in artifacts/registry/relation-kind-registry.json; detailed dedupe/scope/conflict semantics in models/relation.md §3-§6. Cross-Realm constraint: structural relations 'contains' and 'belongs_to' MUST NOT cross Realm (resolved from_ref and to_ref MUST share the same realm_id); weak_semantic=true kinds per the registry MAY cross Realm subject to two-sided authorization. Stays a free string so extension profiles can add kinds; unregistered kinds are opaque edges (unknown_relation_kind), never container/visibility semantics.

rank.description: Top-level rank string for ordered relations (e.g. contains-list-strand position). Encoding follows conformance/encoding.md §9. Aligned with Space.rank so all rank-bearing canonical objects expose rank at the top level instead of fields.rank.

fields.description: Edge metadata. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key — rank moved to the top level in v1 to align with Space.rank.

state.description: Relation state. 'tombstoned' covers both deletion and redaction; the originating reason is preserved on the ak.relation.tombstone / ak.redaction event, not on the materialized object.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.relation.tombstone / redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

object_ref.description: Typed canonical object reference. Allowed kinds: realm, space, actor_profile, strand, message, morph, relation, event, view, blob metadata ID and content-addressed blob ref (sha256 / blake3). Actor endpoints use the structured ActorId branch of relation_endpoint, never a DID or serialized JSON string.

relation_endpoint.description: A typed object-reference string or a structured full ActorId. Equality and deduplication preserve the complete ActorId including Station. This branch represents an actor.

relation_conflict_domain.description: The single primary conflict domain a require_review group and its ak.relation.resolve Control Move address. The Realm is never a member: an Event takes it from its own envelope and a read takes it from the request selector, so one domain can never be spelled two ways. Circle is never a component either (models/relation.md §6). domain_kind is the registered primary_conflict_domain of the matching relation-kind-registry.json shape and is not producer-selectable: tuple keys on (relation_kind, from_ref, to_ref) and from keys on (relation_kind, from_ref). truth_source shapes have no directly writable Relation and therefore no resolvable domain.

relation_kind.description: The relation_kind of every candidate in the group. It MUST resolve to a directly writable relation-kind-registry.json shape whose registered primary_conflict_domain equals domain_kind; a derived_projection shape is rejected with schema_violation (reason=relation_kind_contains_derived / relation_kind_watches_derived).

to_ref.description: Present exactly when domain_kind=tuple. A from domain already contains every duplicate tuple under the same from_ref, so carrying to_ref there would create a second, independently adjudicable sub-group.

relation_conflict_baseline.description: The frozen data-plane candidate baseline a Relation conflict resolution is signed against. authority_revision freezes governance state only, so it never proves that every Relation ordinary Event in the group was observed; this object is the separate data-plane commitment. members_digest is the chained commitment defined in zh/models/relation.md §6.3 and binds realm, domain, member_count, the canonical member ordering and every member. A root, a count or a handful of inclusion proofs on their own do not prove the absence of an omitted member.

member_count.description: Complete number of active candidate heads in the domain under this baseline. It is NOT bounded by the ordinary 16-head diagnostic limit: a group that exceeded the diagnostic fanout is still repaired through this same carrier.

members_digest.description: Chained complete-set commitment over the canonically ordered member list (zh/models/relation.md §6.3).

member_event_ids.description: Complete canonical member list, bytewise-ascending and duplicate-free. Present exactly when member_count <= 64 so a small group stays self-contained; above that the Event carries only members_digest and the material is read page by page through ak.self.relation_conflicts.read.candidates.v1 instead of growing an unbounded Event.

relation_conflict_material_page.description: One page of the frozen repair material. A page never takes effect on its own: the reader MUST walk every page in ascending page_index, recompute page_digest over the chain, and only then compare the final chain value with baseline.members_digest. prev_page_digest chains the pages so a dropped, reordered or duplicated page cannot pass unnoticed.

prev_page_digest.description: page_digest of page_index-1. Absent exactly on page_index=0, where the canonical preimage encodes null.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page. A resumed read continues from this cursor and MUST restart from page_index=0 when the chain no longer matches (relation_conflict_material_page_gap).

relation_conflict_candidates_request_bod.description: Request body of ak.self.relation_conflicts.read.candidates.v1. The caller names one Realm and one primary conflict domain; the receiving Station verifies the caller's read authorization over every candidate in the group before returning any page.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previously returned page. Absent on the first request, which always returns page_index=0.

relation_conflict_candidates_outcome.description: Server-validated result of ak.self.relation_conflicts.read.candidates.v1. The client trusts its own Station for candidate completeness and admission (zh/sync/server-trusted-results.md) and only checks that the echoed selector matches what it asked for, that the page chain is intact and that the final chain value equals baseline.members_digest before signing an ak.relation.resolve against it. This outcome is projection-only evidence: reducer_input MUST be false.

diagnostic.description: The ordinary require_review diagnostic, present exactly when baseline.member_count is 2..16. Its absence above 16 removes the display shortcut, never the repair path.

relation_conflict_diagnostic.description: Projection-only require_review diagnostic containing the complete bounded concurrent head set. reducer_input MUST be false; MUST NOT be treated as canonical event bytes, a winner, or dedupe authority. heads is bounded at 16 because that is the ordinary projection/display bound of one diagnostic, NOT a statement that a domain holds at most 16 candidates and NOT a bound on repair evidence: the 17th and every later candidate is retained, and relation_conflict_baseline carries an unbounded member_count for the same domain. See zh/models/relation.md §6.

conflict_domain.description: The typed primary conflict domain these candidates collided under. It replaces the former opaque dedupe_key string so a producer can neither invent a bucket nor bypass the registered mutual-exclusion shape.

heads.description: Complete canonical concurrent head set, sorted by event_id for wire stability only. No member is a winner or loser.

reason.description: Optional reason code for this candidate's disposition (e.g. relation_conflict_fanout_exceeded).
